newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK unemployment data published at 0930 GMT which showed unemployment fell by 40,800 in October, (vs expected -25,000), average earnings up 4.0 pct in September as expected and unit wage costs up 5.2 pct (vs expected 4.5 pct).

"The market is looking for any evidence of inflation and these are exactly the sort of number to provide that. People are going to ask is that quarter point rate rise enough so the market is going to get very bullish now about further interest rate rises."
"I'm not overly surprised at the numbers because they are consistent with the economy picking up. But the real worry for the market will be the big increase coming through in unit labour costs.

"I think on the assumption the budget is relatively tight, I'd just about come down on the side of steady interest rates in front of the election...But I admit in the light of today's numbers...and if we see additional strength coming through in tomorrow's RPI numbers, we will almost certainly have to see another 25 bps rise before polling day itself."

"The very large fall in unemployment plus upward revision to last month's numbers was right at the top end of expectations. Positive for sterling and negative for gilts and short sterling. Although average earnings remained unchanged, the pressures are now clearly upwards. The unit labour costs data weren't so good on a year on year basis. Taken together, these numbers will certainly maintain Bank of England pressure for further rate rises in the months before the budget."

"The unemployment fall is a big shock - part of that is distorted by the jobseekers allowance which is estimated to account for about a 10,000 fall, so even if you strip that out it's still above expectations. It does seem the labour market is pretty buoyant. There was a large rise in manufacturing employment which underlines the recovery in that sector. The data underline the overall recovery is becoming quite punchy.
Interest rates are going to go up early next year, the pressure is on for a 25 point rise before the election. It does make the case for a rate rise that much clearer."
